title: Snap a scored wall tile over a rod
instruction: The tile is scored across its middle. Snap it in two along the score over the steel rod, without lifting it off the rod, then let go.
context: Tile and stone setters (O*NET 47-2044.00) snap scored wall tiles by laying the score over a nail or rod and pressing both halves down at once. Pressing one side only tips the whole tile on the rod. Unlike other pressing or pulling tasks, here the part is broken by bending: the two hands must hold both ends down while the middle is supported by a line.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Cutting board: plywood, 20 x 32 x 1.2 cm, centred at x 29, y 0. Rod: steel, 8 mm diameter, 14 cm long, along x at y 0 on the board (top 2.0 cm above the table). Tile: glazed ceramic wall tile, 10 x 24 x 0.7 cm, 0.38 kg, scored across its middle (along x) with a groove cut from the glazed face to leave a 1.0 mm web (see the real-world build), so that it snaps at about 3 N pressed down on each end; two 0.19 kg halves joined along the score, laid on the rod with the score 1 mm toward +y of the rod's top, so the +y end rests on the board and the -y end is raised about 1.5 cm.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and photos. A clean snap means: exactly two pieces, the fracture within 2 mm of the score line across the whole 10 cm width, and no chip wider than 3 mm missing from either edge. In simulation the halves cannot chip, so the two things that cause a ragged break are checked instead: a finger within 6 cm of the score at the moment of the snap, or the score more than 3 mm from the rod's top line before it. 0 if the tile never snaps, or a piece leaves the board (for good). 0.25 if it snaps but not cleanly (kept for good). 0.5 if it snaps cleanly but at the end a gripper is within 3 cm of a piece, a piece is not lying on the board, or the pieces are still moving. 1.0 if it snaps cleanly, both pieces lie on the board, both grippers are at least 3 cm from them, and the pieces move less than 1 mm for the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Take a fresh tile from the prepared batch (same box, grooved to the same 1.0 mm web) and lay it glazed face up on the rod with the score 1 mm toward +y of the rod's top, the +y end on the board; centre the board on its outline. In simulation the two halves are put back together.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The tile is two boxes on a hinge along the score, ends-down only, spring 6 N m/rad (about 3 N at 0.10 m from the rod bends it 3 degrees). At 3 degrees a script makes the break permanent: the halves stay joined by the hinge, whose drive is then driven toward a new target (9.7 degrees, about 1.5 N per half) so they lean down onto the board. Nothing fractures or chips, so a ragged break is judged from its causes. The board is a 30 kg rigid body. No contact force cap.
